subject: Post-call recap: VPC / on-prem constraints & priorities
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Irene Quinn <irene.quinn@cedarcare.com>, Tom Hastings <thastings@cedarcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: VPC / on-prem constraints & priorities

Hi Irene / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can prioritize next steps on both sides. I’ve kept this high level — flag anything I miss.

Summary of pain and goals
- Data residency: CedarCare must keep PHI and derived text embeddings within US regions (primary: US-VA). No cross-border backups.
- Regulatory driver: state health regulations + upcoming audit; procurement is prioritizing SOC2-compatible evidence and auditable logs.
- Deployment preference: strong bias toward private hosting (VPC + private control plane) or fully on-prem air-gapped stack for prod workloads with a self-managed control plane.
- Network constraints: restrictive egress policy — only allowlisted outbound to a small set of endpoints; no persistent outbound to general public internet from inference nodes.
- Security asks: KMS/HSM integration for key custody, customer-managed logging (forwarded to your SIEM), and an auditable access log for inference requests.
- Performance ask: sub-300ms median token latency for authentication + small prompt paths during pilot targets; final SLO to be defined.

Timeline and priority
- Pilot: aim to start a small POC in Oct 2026 (one model, limited traffic).
- Production: target Jan 2027 for gated production rollout pending security sign-off and procurement.

Open technical constraints (what we need from CedarCare)
1) Network diagram showing egress restrictions, proxy requirements, and any private peering options.
2) Firewall/allowlist process & contacts — who on infra can accept the list of endpoints and certs?
3) KMS/HSM provider and whether we can run an HSM inside your colo/VPC or use a private HSM proxy.
4) Any air-gap requirements for the control plane (if you require fully air-gapped control plane we’ll need to discuss an on-prem console + offline updates flow).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Lauren (Redwood) -> Share short MOP (mutual action plan) and sample SOW draft by Fri 2026-08-21. Attachment: redwood-sample-soc2-evidence.pdf
- Priyom (Redwood) -> Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/network team (please propose two 60-min slots).
- CedarCare -> Share network diagram & firewall contact (we referenced one placeholder doc; please send the authoritative diagram). Attachment: cedarcare-vpc-drawings.pdf (if available)

Attachments shared with this message: redwood-sample-soc2-evidence.pdf (sample evidence pack)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/cedarcare-network-diagram (placeholder)

Thanks again — we’ll stand up the MAP and get Priyom scheduled as soon as you share infra availability.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VPC / on-prem constraints & priorities

Thanks Lauren — this looks good and captures the main points. A few clarifications and items from our side:

Clarifications
- Control plane: we are leaning toward a private control plane hosted in our VPC (preferred) rather than a fully air-gapped console for the pilot. For production, security will evaluate on-prem console options.
- Egress: our infra policy requires that any outbound destinations be approved via a ticket; we cannot allow persistent public outbound except to vendor endpoints approved by the security team.
- KMS: we currently use AWS KMS with an HSM-backed key policy. We will need Redwood to support CMEK integration and accept that keys remain under our KMS.

Questions
1) For the on-prem option, what parts of the Redwood stack still require periodic outbound connectivity (if any)? We need a short list of control-plane endpoints and ports.
2) Do you provide a mechanism for offline model updates (i.e., air-gapped push via signed bundles) if we move to a stricter on-prem stance?
3) Can you provide a sample list of the logs/audit events Redwood will produce (request-level metadata, identity, timestamps) so we can map to our SIEM fields?

I attached a concise network policy snapshot we use internally (cedarcare-network-snip.pdf). For scheduling the deep dive, our infra lead (Tom) is available 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-27 in the morning EST.

We’ll also loop procurement once we have a rough SOW and estimate. Procurement expects a draft by early Sep.

Thanks — Irene
